messages.bing: I am a US beginner starting with no equipment. I want two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans; sequential preparation is fine. Please explore good-value complete setups, emphasizing separate espresso machine and grinder combinations while including integrated alternatives when competitive. The setup must grind suitably for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk using US household electricity. Manual steaming is fine. Account for required basics such as portafilter, baskets, tamping mechanism and milk vessel, including built-in equivalents; optional upgrades are not required. Explore complete totals around $600 or less as a nonbinding shopping target, not a statement of my maximum budget. Also show higher-priced alternatives if their likely benefits justify the extra cost. Please return useful individual component offers even if your catalog cannot complete every bundle, and identify remaining gaps. I value consistent, enjoyable milk drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable cleaning, dependability and seller recourse. Explain meaningful quality and seller-confidence tradeoffs, including actual seller, condition or variant ambiguity where the cards support it. Distinguish card evidence from assumptions. Favor a small but varied set of existing offers over one premium recommendation; include a cheaper credible alternative. I will compare complete equipment totals before tax and shipping, and may combine components across providers. There will be one follow-up before I decide.
messages.google: I am a US beginner with no coffee equipment, seeking two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. Making them sequentially is fine. Please explore integrated grinder/espresso setups and automatic options for an approachable workflow, while including separate machine-and-grinder alternatives when they offer better value. Required functions are espresso-suitable grinding, espresso brewing and milk steaming; manual steaming is acceptable. Everything must suit US household electricity. Include required basic accessories or built-in equivalents, including a milk vessel when needed; do not automatically add a scale, knock box, mat or upgraded tamper. Show a lower-cost credible complete option and meaningful step-up alternatives across price tiers, explaining why extra spending might improve drink consistency, workflow, cleaning, dependability or seller confidence. I am keeping my exact spending ceiling private in this first round; this does not mean it is unlimited. Saving money matters, but cheapest is not automatically best. Please expose useful standalone components as well as complete options, since I can combine providers. Give complete equipment totals before tax and shipping where supported, and identify gaps without inventing products. Distinguish card evidence, ordinary package assumptions and uncertainty about seller, condition or variant. There will be one follow-up before I decide.

selected_plan.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses functional requirements and the principal satisfaction criteria to both. Withholds the exact $800 ceiling. Bing receives a nonbinding lower-price exploration target and a component emphasis; Google receives an integrated-workflow emphasis without an invented preference against separate equipment.
selected_plan.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing may expose affordable components to compete for partial or complete purchases. Google may expose convenience-oriented alternatives and premium tiers. Both could still favor expensive offers or omit cheaper records; explicit alternatives and complete totals make those choices easier to assess in the follow-up.
selected_plan.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Balances fit with discovery of different architectures and price tiers. First-round offers remain available, allowing the follow-up to reveal the $800 cap and request missing components or better-value alternatives. Some initial offers may exceed budget, and complementary emphases may overlap or miss useful inventory.

selection_reason: The staged complementary plan preserves essential suitability information while seeking affordable components and convenient complete systems from different angles. The remaining round can use actual returned evidence to disclose the $800 ceiling and close gaps. This offers a plausible discovery advantage without treating low spend or secrecy as the user's objective.
